performance_claim_scope: The sequential committed-production comparison is sufficient to reject promotion because the candidate loses repeated decode and increases tracked plus whole-GTT peak at both required long-context rows. It is not published as a retained A/B speed claim.
correctness_claim_scope: The fixed 8-BF16/2-INT8 full-attention map passes the committed 11-prompt 4K/16 gate (ten category/train/heldout prompts plus mixed_v1) on gfx1151 with a 65,792-token resident allocation, no persistent BF16 mirror, and released layer-local prefill-oracle buffers.

source.tracked_status_at_measurement: Only unrelated docs/ROCM-AI.md was modified; runtime, kernel, benchmark, quality-harness, and K1 test sources matched the commit.
source.untracked_qualification: Pre-existing untracked benchmark outputs were excluded from this artifact and all hashes.

candidate.prefill_oracle_lifetime: One layer-local BF16 K/V pair is allocated while prefill consumes each compact layer and released afterward.
candidate.existing_mode_disposition: Keep the existing guarded/explicit hybrid path and exact BF16 fallback; do not promote it over the gfx1151 BF16 default or claim a speed/memory win.

closed_prior_frontier: All-layer per-token/head and pure-INT8 policies have prompt-dependent strict-quality failures.
Three-INT8-layer prefix-7 and non-contiguous {5,8,9}/{6,8,9} K+V maps fail the established long quality gate.
Key-only prefix-6 fails; passing prefix-7 key-only saves less than the two-layer K+V map.
Tail-four Hadamard group32 is quality-clean on gfx1100 but loses repeated decode and allocator high water.
These rows were not repeated under SH-K1.

protocol.quality: BF16 reference and candidate run in independent resident sessions over all ten committed natural prompts (including four category heldouts) plus mixed_v1. Each prompt contributes the prompt-final row plus 16 teacher-forced decode rows with identical token histories.
protocol.wall_memory: Independent right-sized candidate processes at 32K/128 and 64K/128, one discarded run plus three measured runs, eager decode, cached builds, one hardware queue, and simultaneous 10-ms whole-device GTT sampling. The committed SH-M2 owner-slot BF16 rows are the production baseline.
protocol.profile: Cached full-process rocprofv3 kernel traces at 32K and 64K with one prefill, one warmup transition, and four measured transitions. Selected-region gating was not used because the installed libroctx64 lacks roctxProfilerResume/Pause; the decode-only INT8 grouped-GQA symbol keeps the producer count unambiguous.
protocol.promotion_rule: Require quality thresholds, no persistent BF16 mirror in compact layers, repeated decode and memory wins, <=1% prefill loss, and valid grouped-GQA traces at both 32K and 64K.

validation.focused_tests: 237 passed: KV dispatch/policy/spans, GGUF INT8 policy, memory audit, E2E fixture gate, mixed-KV suite, and resident batch layout
validation.hip_decode_smoke: 3/3 cases passed; max abs <=2.98e-08 including split/page-boundary and fp16-scale cases

decision.production_default: BF16 KV with SH-M2 owner-slot scratch
decision.conclusion: The fixed 8/2 hybrid is strict-quality-safe on gfx1151 and the intended direct grouped-GQA consumer is active, but it is neither a repeated decode win nor a peak-memory win. Its persistent saving is smaller than the required layer-local BF16 prefill-oracle high water. Close SH-K1 without changing production and advance to SH-A1.
